items.definition:
providing an advantage; favorable
It would be advantageous to start early.

Relating to dogs.
The veterinarian specializes in canine diseases.

Relating to cause and effect.
There is a causal link between smoking and lung cancer.

Not having enough of a specified quality or ingredient.
The soil was deficient in essential nutrients.

Shockingly bad; unacceptable.
His behavior was absolutely disgraceful.

Strange and frightening.
The old house had an eerie silence.

desperate or wild with fear, anxiety, or other emotion
She was frantic with worry when her child didn't come home.

lacking kindness or sympathy; cruel
It was a heartless act to leave the dog alone in the cold.

relating to or denoting hormones
She felt very emotional due to hormonal changes.

Melted, especially by heat.
The molten lava flowed slowly down the volcano.

Richly luxurious and soft.
The hotel room had a plush carpet and comfortable furniture.

easy to understand and feel sympathy for
Her struggles made her character very relatable to the audience.

containing salt
The doctor prescribed a saline solution for the patient's eyes.

having a mild climate; showing moderation or self-restraint
The temperate climate of the region is ideal for agriculture.

relating to a particular theme or subject
The exhibition had a strong thematic focus on environmental issues.

relating to electromagnetic radiation beyond the violet end of the visible spectrum
Ultraviolet rays can be harmful to the skin.

showing no prejudice for or against something; impartial
We need an unbiased opinion on this matter.

not having undergone a process or treatment
The untreated water was not safe to drink.

unjust or illegal
He was accused of wrongful dismissal.

relating to the way a person or animal behaves
She studies human behavioral patterns.

dishonest or unreliable
That car looks a bit dodgy; I wouldn't buy it.

relating to the earth or human life
He had no earthly idea what she was talking about.

optional; chosen by election
Students can choose two elective courses this semester.

relating to the intestines
The doctor diagnosed an intestinal infection.

showing wild excitement and energy
He was in a manic state after drinking too much coffee.

able to be measured
We need to set measurable goals for the project.

quiet, gentle, and easily imposed on
Despite his meek appearance, he was a very strong leader.

pleasantly smooth or soft; relaxed and good-humored
The wine had a mellow flavor, perfect for dinner.

willing to consider or accept new suggestions and ideas
She was very receptive to new ideas for the project.

treating complex issues and problems as if they are much simpler than they really are
His explanation of the problem was too simplistic.

relating to supervision
She has a supervisory role in the department.

dangerous; disloyal
The mountain path was treacherous after the storm.

forming a united whole
The team presented a cohesive argument.

serving to explain something
The document included an explanatory note.

relating to or caused by a fungus
He was treated for a fungal infection.

behaving in a way that suggests one has higher standards or more noble beliefs than is the case
It's hypocritical to criticize others for something you do yourself.

very poor or bad
I had a lousy day at work.

not aware of or not concerned about what is happening around one
He seemed oblivious to the danger.

obvious; not secret
He showed overt hostility towards the new policy.

devoutly religious
She was known for her pious devotion to her faith.

smooth and continuous, without apparent breaks or transitions
The transition between the two scenes was seamless.

causing nausea or disgust
The smell from the garbage was sickening.

excessively self-satisfied or complacent
He had a smug look on his face after winning.

not flowing or moving; showing no activity
The stagnant water in the pond attracted mosquitoes.

not replied to or solved
Many questions remained unanswered after the press conference.

not morally correct
His business practices were considered unethical.

relating to urine or the organs that produce and excrete it
The doctor examined the patient's urinary system.

serving to prove a case; decisive or convincing
The evidence was conclusive; he was guilty.

characterized by refined taste and good education
He is a very cultured man, well-traveled and knowledgeable.

relating to or causing depression; gloomy
She was experiencing a depressive episode.

producing good or helpful results; productive
We had a very fruitful discussion about the project.

relating to the stomach
He suffered from a gastric ulcer.

unable to be reached or entered
The remote village was almost inaccessible in winter.

Liable to be punished.
Fraud is a serious offense, punishable by law.

concerned more with the needs and wishes of others than with one's own
Her selfless dedication to the charity was admirable.

full of or covered with stones; unfeeling or cold
He gave me a stony glare when I interrupted him.

not solved or ended
The conflict remained unresolved for many years.

not stated or determined precisely
The package arrived at an unspecified time.

relating to Venice or its people
She admired the beautiful Venetian glass.

relating to a consul or consulate
You can get help from the consular office if you lose your passport abroad.

intended to correct or improve something
The company took corrective action to fix the problem.

done quickly and without careful thought
He made a hasty decision he later regretted.

strong and sturdy; or a deep, rough voice
He had a husky voice after shouting all day.

not qualified
Due to his age, he was ineligible to participate in the competition.
